15 See that none render evil for evil unto any man; but ever follow that which is good, both among yourselves, and to all men. (1 Thessalonians 5:15 KJV)

This is telling us to never render evil back unto any man, no matter what they do to you, as you should always render good back unto those who treat you bad. Our human nature will try to get us to always strike back at those that offend us, but that is not what us Christians are supposed to do. If you are walking in the Spirit you can overcome your natural desires to strike back at people. Paul gave this same principal in Romans (Romans 12:17, 21), and Peter said it (1 Peter 3:9). This principal was given by Jesus (Matthew 5:39-44 & Luke 6:27-29).

Paul is instructing the followers to treat ALL men the same, showing good, not evil, to everyone, and not just to fellow believers. Paul says to be especially good to fellow believers (Galatians 6:10). If we are to be like Jesus, we will show the love of God to all people that we have contact with, as He told us to “Love our neighbor as ourselves” (Matthew 22:39). Neighbor means everyone, not just your physical neighbors. You don’t have the love of God in your heart, if you don’t show love to your neighbor. You must realize that you first have to let God love you, as you can not give away what you don’t have. Many Christians have never experienced the love of God being poured out on them, so they are unable to give it to others. Let the Word teach you that God is love (1 John 4:8), so that you will be able to show that kind of love to others. Wouldn’t it be wonderful if this whole world would just love each other, as Jesus told us to? If you are born again, you have God’s love in your heart as part of the fruit of the Spirit (Galatians 5:22-23). Praise God for His Love!

Devotional by Pastor Joe W. Green, www.Infinite-Faith.com

As someone who edits video for youtube, vimeo, and dailymotion channels you need to be careful on what you get yourself into.

One. Don't make any deals to become part of a network for the promise of added subs. They usually want you to become part of their network so they can take away part of your ad revenue under the guise of a contract. This is super sketchy and 99% it's a scam.

Two. Don't make any deals to get involved in product placement. There are very strict laws about making fake reviews and product placement with and without disclosure. Depending on your country you could get royally fucked legally speaking.

Three. If your not entertaining people won't watch you no matter what products you show. If you don't have a hook for your channel and you do the same copy/paste reviews everyone else is doing you will only be competing for clicks based on the product itself. Also 10k is pretty low to start even if you have $500-$1000 a month in ad revenue from that it's a dangerous investment. Get yourself a solid hook or gimmick. Make it fun and don't be super serious. If your just another mouth breather huffing over the same shit 1000 other people are it won't go very far.

Forth. Stay independent but don't shy away from collaborative content. Working with other channels is good as is networking however you should remain your own thing. Keep your own ad revenue yet sharing subscribers and viewers is a good thing to do. The people who start drama and other bullshit yet have a massive fallowing are there only because of luck. One guy makes a semi-viral video doing something stupid then just has a channel of them talking over a longplay about another dumb youtuber despite never creating any real content yet staying profitable is INCREDIBLY RARE. Stay on topic but make what your doing positive and entertaining. The majority of youtubers aren't into negative content it just so happens that the hypercritically negative youtubers we have are incredibly vocal and annoying. So play nice, other people will be more willing to work with you if you do.

You definitely have a good chance of starting up though. Your best place to start might be investing in a DSLR or Camcorder for video that can do 1080p at 60FPS. Amazon and a few other places sell kits with extra batteries, lights, filters, microphones, and memory cards for under $1000. I also noticed you videos have been getting better compared to your older releases, editing, content, and the character has definitely improved. Filling in the dull stuff with music, commentary, and voice overs is always a win. And not to be too harsh but the earlier videos are a bit home movie like compared to the road trip stuff that's been getting you views. And don't just focus on the road and the cars on these trip videos though. If you end up someplace weird don't be afraid to show it off, you can definitely attract viewers who are into travel vids and not just the muscle cars. Seriously if you stop someplace cool like a wacky museum or an alligator farm make an effort to present that in your trips. It's obvious that the car can take you places just make it more apparent that there are stops along the way that aren't gas stations. It feels a bit claustrophobic to watch.
